dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Golden Nara is the same color as Nara Varuna in the story. Whose story do you want to listen to?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Aramuhukunda's story.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: In the most ancient stories, Aramuhukunda had already left his mark.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Perhaps Aramuhukunda appeared first, then there were stories.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: In Aramuhukunda's own story, his enemies were Big Iron Chunks that could block out the sun and cut off rivers. There was also Marana that could turn Vana into Valuka.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: But Aramuhukunda and his partner Aradasha, together with the Golden Nara Varuna, defeated the monsters that Aranara could not defeat.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: However, after that, Aramuhukunda was just a story, and not in Vanarana anymore.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Perhaps he went to a place far, far away with Nara Varuna.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Perhaps he was summoned to the side of Queen Aranyani.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Perhaps he stepped alone on the path to facing the ruler of Valuka.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: #But because his story still exists, Aramuhukunda is still in Vanarana. The rivers know him, the trees know him, and even Nara {NICKNAME} now knows him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Go, Golden Nara. Nara's time is very precious after all.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: #Nara {NICKNAME} brought us many, many stories. Do you want to hear other stories?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Queen Aranyani's story.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: All Aranara are children of Queen Aranyani, even Aramuhukunda.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Queen Aranyani loves all living things in Vana equally, whether they are Aranara, Nara, Mushrooms, or Rishboland Tigers... To Queen Aranyani, all of them are green leaves on the same tree. Whether they are from the crown of the tree, or from the lowest branches, the leaves plucked from the tree all have the same shape.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: So all living things returned the same love to Queen Aranyani.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: But one day, the sky turned black and the streams became as acrid as blood... Big iron chunks and large ink-black monsters were everywhere. The forest started burning too, and Marana flowed out like spring water.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: In order to heal the world, Queen Aranyani went to a place far, far away. However, she did not return. Perhaps she turned into a tree to bear fruit that can heal the world.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Many Aranara only knew what the taste of sadness was like for the first time when that happened.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The ruler of Valuka's story.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: What an embarrassment... Even Arakarman might not know much about the ruler of Valuka's story.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: But Arakarman knows that the Nara of Valuka are stronger than the Nara of Vana.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Then the ruler of Valuka must be a very amazing ruler, even if they were not as powerful as Queen Aranyani. I heard that he built stone pillars higher than the tallest trees in Valuka.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: But after that, Arakarman did not hear much about the ruler of Valuka.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Because bad Marana appeared in Vana, Aranara were unwilling to hear anymore about Valuka.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: After many sunrises and moonrises, very few Aranara know that even Valuka had a ruler.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Aradasha's story.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Oh! Oooh! Arakarman likes Aradasha's story the most! Many Aranara like it too.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Before Aradasha, only Queen Aranyani's Ararakalari was stronger than his. After Aradasha, Aradasha's Ararakalari was the strongest.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: But Aradasha was not powerful from the time he was a seed.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Aradasha cultivated slowly, starting from destroying mushrooms, all the way to shattering Big Iron Chunks. He defeated eighteen bad guys in total.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: And every time he defeated a bad guy, there would be another story, so Aradasha's stories are the most numerous.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Even weak Arakarman wants to cultivate Ararakalari after hearing these stories of training.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Later, Aradasha joined Aramuhukunda's adventure, and had the story that all Aranara know. In the blink of an eye, the big metal monsters were dealt with.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: But soon after, the birds and the flying flowers could find no trace of him. He must have gone with Aramuhukunda, to a place far, far away.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Arakarman
dialogues.text: Go, Golden Nara. Let new stories grow.
